Female imagoes of Coccinella septempunctata emerge with a mean body length of 0.765 cm  and a body width of 0.591 cm , dimensions that establish the baseline morphology for the adult stage. The wet weight of these newly emerged females averages 0.0388 grams , a value that represents the culmination of larval mass accumulation. When larvae are reared on the pea aphid Acyrthosiphon pisum, the duration from hatch to pupation is 8.9 days  at a constant temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C]. The freshly formed pupa under these conditions weighs 0.0415 grams , though an alternative pupal wet weight of 0.01505 grams  has also been reported in the literature, likely reflecting differences in larval diet or measurement timing.

Larval development proceeds through four distinct instars, each characterized by stepwise increases in body mass. First instars, immediately after the onset of exogenous feeding, have a wet weight of 0.00226 grams [Ww0 = 0.00226 grams]. This value rises to 0.00555 grams  by the second instar and to 0.01063 grams  by the third instar. The fourth and final larval instar reaches a mean wet weight of 0.01979 grams , reflecting nearly a tenfold increase from the first instar. The eggs from which these larvae hatch, when provisioned on Myzus persicae, have an initial wet weight of 0.000187 grams [Ww0 = 0.000187 grams], a modest starting mass that belies the rapid growth trajectory of the species. If growth were to continue without the cessation imposed by metamorphosis, the hypothetical asymptotic adult wet weight would be 0.08 grams , a figure that highlights the substantial physiological constraint imposed by the transition to the imaginal stage.

Body size and mass continue to change during the early adult phase, particularly in females. After 14 days of feeding on Acyrthosiphon pisum, one cohort of females exhibited a body length of 0.769 cm  and a body width of 0.588 cm , with a corresponding wet weight of 0.039 grams . A separate group of 14-day-old females, also consuming the same aphid prey, displayed slightly different dimensions, with a body length of 0.72 cm  and a width of 0.552 cm . By 24 days post-emergence, the body length of females on this diet had increased slightly to 0.756 cm , while the width remained relatively stable at 0.555 cm . At 21 days old, the wet weight of these older females had risen to 0.0659 grams , and by 24 days it was 0.0658 grams , suggesting that mass gain plateaus or fluctuates modestly during the first weeks of adult life.

The dry-weight-specific feeding rates of larvae and adults, measured at 27 °C [T = 27 °C] using the mustard aphid Lipaphis erysimi as prey, increase markedly across development. In the first instar, the ingestion rate, expressed as joules per gram of dry body weight per day, is 25020 J per day per gram  at a temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. This value rises to 29832 J per day per gram  in the second instar and further to 37196 J per gram per day  in the third instar at a temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C] at a temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. The fourth instar achieves a rate of 37321 J per gram per day , a figure nearly identical to that of the third instar, indicating a possible plateau before pupation at a temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. Upon reaching the imaginal stage, the adult feeding rate climbs substantially to 49162 J per gram per day , reflecting the heightened metabolic demands of reproduction and dispersal at a temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C].

Development times are highly sensitive to temperature, with clear thermal optima evident across the larval instars. At 23 °C [T = 23 °C], the first instar lasts 3.1 days , the second 2.2 days , the third 2.4 days , and the fourth 5.4 days . Elevating the temperature to 24 °C [T = 24 °C] shortens these durations: instar one takes 2.0 days , instar two also 2.0 days , instar three 2.47 days , and instar four 2.29 days . At 25 °C [T = 25 °C], durations continue to decline: instar one is 1.72 days , instar two 1.64 days , instar three 1.84 days , and instar four 2.75 days . At 28 °C [T = 28 °C], the first instar lasts 1.76 days , the second 1.8 days , the third 2.4 days , and the fourth 3.15 days . Female imago lifespan likewise varies with temperature: The longevity of the female imago, measured from adult emergence, was 48.16 days  at 24 °C [T = 24 °C] and feeding on Rhopalosiphum padi, whereas the lifespan from adult emergence at 28 °C [T = 28 °C] was sharply reduced to 26.74 days , illustrating the physiological cost of higher metabolic rates.
